name: Hammerfall

angles.text: Hammerfall stands as a solemn monument to the liberation of the orcish internment camps and the sacrifice of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer.
For orcs, the fall of Doomhammer in Arathi is one of the most painful moments in their history, marking the end of an era and the rise of Thrall's new Horde.
Orgrim Doomhammer remains an iconic warrior of legend, and walking the grounds where he fell in battle carries heavy martial significance.

faq.answer: Gor'mul was an orc captive held in the internment camp that once stood where Hammerfall now rests. Although Thrall and Doomhammer led an assault to liberate the camp, Gor'mul was left behind in the chaotic escape and wandered alone for years in despair.

Orgrim Doomhammer was slain during the battle to liberate the Arathi internment camp. While leading the attack in his black plate armor, he was struck from behind by an Alliance knight charging on horseback who ran him through with a lance.

The outpost was named Hammerfall in honor of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, who fell at this exact location while freeing his people from human captivity. The Horde later returned to the ruined camp to establish a permanent base.
faq.q: Why is the outpost named Hammerfall?

faq.answer: Tor'gan is a Horde representative stationed in Hammerfall who helps look after the encampment and understands the lingering trauma suffered by former captives like Gor'mul.

Yes. Thrall fought alongside Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer in the assault on this Arathi internment camp. Together, they shattered the camp's defenses to liberate the captive orcs, though the victory came at the cost of Doomhammer's life.
faq.q: Did Thrall take part in the battle here?

faq.answer: Gor'mul witnessed Doomhammer struck down before his eyes, crushing his spirit. When the other captives escaped into the wilderness, he was left behind, wandering aimlessly without hope until the Horde returned to build Hammerfall.

sections.body: Hammerfall was once a grim Alliance internment camp where captive orcs were kept behind wood and steel after the Second War. That changed when young Thrall and Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer launched an assault to shatter the enclosures and free their kin. Though the raid succeeded in freeing many captives and bringing down the camp's defenses, it ended in tragedy when Doomhammer was struck from behind by a mounted lance, dying on the very soil where the Horde settlement now stands.
sections.title: Blood and Broken Chains

sections.body: Not every captive found freedom on that fateful day. In the chaos of battle and the tremors of the earth, an orc named Gor'mul watched the legendary Warchief fall and lost all will to fight. Left behind as his brethren fled, Gor'mul spent years wandering the highlands in directionless grief. Even now that the Horde has reclaimed the site as a fortified base, the memory of that cowardly strike continues to haunt those who survived it.
sections.title: The Lingering Shadow of Defeat

summary: Hammerfall recounts the tragic fall of Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer during the liberation of an Alliance internment camp in the Arathi Highlands. Through the grief-stricken memories of Gor'mul, travelers learn how the camp was freed and why the stronghold bears its solemn name.
